description: constraints.golang is an exact version so that Renovate installs the Go that postUpgradeTasks need without looking its releases up on GitHub, which takes a token Renovate here does not have.

packageRules.description: Every pin moves in one pull request, and that pull request is the release: postUpgradeTasks notes the pins in CHANGELOG.md and cuts the version, and the merge starts the release workflow. Renovate merges it itself, on a run that finds every check of the test workflow green. platformAutomerge is off because Renovate promises that only of its own automerge: a platform's, on a branch with no required checks, may merge sooner. The schedule opens no pull request in the last hour of the UTC day: the version is dated when it is cut, and the release workflow publishes nothing dated another day than its merge.
The base is a dated snapshot, trixie-YYYYMMDD. Renovate's debian versioning reads the codename as release 13 and drops the date.
GO_VERSION is pinned in an ARG, which the annotation above it moves; the dockerfile manager sees the same pin through the FROM lines and cannot write it.
Of go.mod Renovate moves the changelog tool and the go directive, below; the rest of it is not Renovate's.

The changelog tool that postUpgradeTasks runs is a tool of go.mod. It is no part of the image: its move is a pull request of its own, with no changelog entry and no release. Renovate merges it on green checks like the pins, though no check runs the tool.

The go directive follows Go's patch releases and is one of the pins: it moves in their pull request and their release. The test workflow gates it: it vets and tests with the Go the directive names, and its image build fails while the directive is ahead of GO_VERSION.
In go.mod Renovate moves patches only: a new minor or major, of Go or of the changelog tool, is a person's decision.
